To be in the water and not to get wet; to go through the fire and not to be burned--these are opposite, irreconcilable conditions. selected.text: Know ye that trials and tribulations have, from time immemorial, been the lot of the chosen Ones of God and His beloved, and such of His servants as are detached from all else but Him, they whom neither merchandise nor traffic beguile from the remembrance of the Almighty, they that speak not till He hath spoken, and act according to His commandment. Such is God's method carried into effect of old, and such will it remain in the future. Blessed are the steadfastly enduring, they that are patient under ills and hardships, who lament not over anything that befalleth them, and who tread the path of resignation

selected.text: Center your thoughts in the Well-Beloved, rather than in your own selves.

selected.text: If the whole earth were to be converted into silver and gold, no man who can be said to have truly ascended into the heaven of faith and certitude would deign to regard it, much less to seize and keep it.

selected.text: Night hath succeeded day, and day hath succeeded night, and the hours and moments of your lives have come and gone, and yet none of you hath, for one instant, consented to detach himself from that which perisheth. Bestir yourselves, that the brief moments that are still yours may not be dissipated and lost. Even as the swiftness of lightning your days shall pass, and your bodies shall be laid to rest beneath a canopy of dust.

selected.text: This is not a Cause which may be made a plaything for your idle fancies, nor is it a field for the foolish and faint of heart. By God, this is the arena of insight and detachment, of vision and upliftment, where none may spur on their chargers save the valiant horsemen of the Merciful, who have severed all attachment to the world of being. These, truly, are they that render God victorious on earth, and are the dawning-places of His sovereign might amidst mankind.
selected.reason: Mandatory inclusion: exact selected wording lies in a catalogue-authorized paragraph of this translation version.

selected.text: By the life of Baha! Only he who is severed from the world shall achieve this ultimate grace, he who is a captive of divine love, empty of passion and self, from every aspect true unto his God, humble, lowly, supplicating, in tears, submissive in the presence of the Lord.

selected.text: Expend your every breath of life in this great Cause and dedicate all your days to the service of Baha, so that in the end, safe from loss and deprivation, ye will inherit the heaped-up treasures of the realms above. For the days of a man are full of peril and he cannot rely on so much as a moment more of life; and still the people, who are even as a wavering mirage of illusions, tell themselves that in the end they shall reach the heights. Alas for them! The men of bygone times hugged these same fancies to their breasts, until a wave flicked over them and they returned to dust, and they found themselves excluded and bereft--all save those souls who had freed themselves from self and had flung away their lives in the pathway of God

selected.text: The spring season of life shall turn into the autumn of death, the bright joy of palace halls give way to moonless dark within the tomb. And therefore is none of this worth loving at all, and to this the wise will not anchor his heart.

selected.text: Worship thou God in such wise that if thy worship lead thee to the fire, no alteration in thine adoration would be produced, and so likewise if thy recompense should be paradise. Thus and thus alone should be the worship which befitteth the one True God. Shouldst thou worship Him because of fear, this would be unseemly in the sanctified Court of His presence, and could not be regarded as an act by thee dedicated to the Oneness of His Being. Or if thy gaze should be on paradise, and thou shouldst worship Him while cherishing such a hope, thou wouldst make God’s creation a partner with Him, notwithstanding the fact that paradise is desired by men. … Fire and paradise both bow down and prostrate themselves before God. That which is worthy of His Essence is to worship Him for His sake, without fear of fire, or hope of paradise. … Although when true worship is offered, the worshipper is delivered from the fire, and entereth the paradise of God’s good-pleasure, yet such should not be the motive of his act. However, God’s favor and grace ever flow in accordance with the exigencies of His inscrutable wisdom.

selected.text: Answer: In this day or Dispensation asceticism is of the spiritual type: For spiritual asceticism is correct - is productive of result. On the one hand a man may attain virtues by inherent force of nature or of existence; on the other hand these virtues may be due to the weakness of his nature. For instance, an infant is detached from the world: that severance or detachment is due to its potential weakness. But a wise man having passed the stage of maturity will likewise be detached from the world, and care nothing for the world, but that severance at that stage is indicative of inherent force or strength of character.
selected.reason: Distinguishes mature spiritual detachment from an infant’s lack of worldly capacity.

omitted.text: Detachment and severance are two wings for the flight of those who are captives of self and passion to the atmosphere of nearness and the presence of God.
omitted.reason: The distinction between infant incapacity and mature detachment adds a necessary qualification beyond the familiar two-wings image.

importedAuthorityReview.authorization: Different rendering of authorized paragraph4; supplied wording not authorized.
importedAuthorityReview.finding: Compared AB03757 version58b1c6f422b730c67afb58b85f78880dcd8a2c1946f44913b66d78adba112202 paragraph4, metadata Y4. The authorized wording reads rid thyself of all attachment to the world and turn thy face unto the Kingdom of God; the supplied be thou severed from all attachment to this world is a different, probably historical, rendering. Omit as a short variant of a teaching stated more fully elsewhere; no authority transferred.

importedAuthorityReview.authorization: Different rendering of authorized paragraph4; supplied wording not authorized.
importedAuthorityReview.finding: Compared AB01339 version c91071542bfb11be732b47814ac0617f28e61f0c39e6228a6b776592d6a2c10c paragraph4, metadata Y4. The authorized prayer reads Release me from every bond, and deliver me from every attachment, that I may cherish no desire except Thy good-pleasure; the supplied Free me from every bond … seek naught but Thy good-pleasure is a different translation. Omit; the authorized prayers for detachment are already selected.

importedAuthorityReview.authorization: Authorized prayer paragraph3, with supplied capitalization and spelling differences preserved.
importedAuthorityReview.finding: Compared BH03109 version43da1ec4c5f868c82fc5c2076e6b47dd6082ad2ee147d5e63ce950a6983a4c4e paragraph3, metadata Y. Every word agrees; the supplied Ocean, Bounty, Heaven, Favour, Day-Star and Grace differ only in capitalization and spelling from ocean, bounty, heaven, favor, Daystar and grace, and the closing full stop is absent. Retain mandatorily and preserve approximate status.

importedAuthorityReview.authorization: Different rendering of authorized paragraph2; supplied wording not authorized.
importedAuthorityReview.finding: Compared AB11952 version7082db157709c90aeae4f7280b4de2342fe9b2eef6211386e6512d3c4b1f5140 paragraph2, metadata Y2. The authorized text reads became purified and sanctified from all else save God, she brought forth such a luminous fruit; the supplied sanctified and purified from worldly concerns is a different rendering and stops mid-sentence. Omit rather than present an incomplete variant; no authority transferred.

importedAuthorityReview.authorization: Plotinus quotation; supplied translator unidentified, no Bahai translation authority.
importedAuthorityReview.finding: The supplied reference identifies Enneads VI.9.9, the same treatise read for an earlier guide in the linked edition, whose wording differs from the supplied translation. The translator of the supplied wording has not been established. Omit; the guide's comparative selections are limited to two short scriptural sayings on self-conquest and patience.

importedAuthorityReview.authorization: Historical published translation; authorized status not established.
importedAuthorityReview.finding: The supplied reference TAB.709 identifies Tablets of Abdul-Baha. Current AB01212 version9cae9405c2fd09058a6f492875cf6f28a97972d4e7e1e8b0e4f4324ffddc3753 paragraph6 is a different provisional rendering with blank Authorized metadata. Omit; the same promise of illumination through severance is carried by selected passages.

importedAuthorityReview.authorization: Buddhist scripture in an unidentified English rendering; no Bahai catalogue authorization inferred.
importedAuthorityReview.finding: Dhammapada chapter8 (Sahassa Vagga) verse103, the fourth verse of that chapter, verified in Acharya Buddharakkhita's translation: one who conquers himself is the noblest victor over a thousand times a thousand men. The supplied wording is a different rendering whose translator is not identified. Include as an independent comparative saying with its attribution and wording preserved.

importedAuthorityReview.authorization: Different rendering of authorized paragraph6; supplied historical wording not authorized.
importedAuthorityReview.finding: Compared AB00044 version e714112f152a1e802acf43807ca710731938dd8550bc210ad59353280775f471 paragraph6, metadata Y4-13,16-. The authorized Selections35 wording begins O army of God! Whensoever ye behold a person whose entire attention is directed toward the Cause of God; the supplied TAB.042 text is a different historical translation. Omit; the theme of confirmation through selfless service is represented by selected passages.

importedAuthorityReview.authorization: Verified published original English written on behalf of Shoghi Effendi.
importedAuthorityReview.finding: The reproduction of The Unfolding Destiny of the British Bahai Community, letter of22 October1949 written on behalf of Shoghi Effendi, pages456–457, contains the supplied sentence as its first item: patience with others and with one's own self, remembering that even the Prophets of God sometimes got tired and cried out in despair. The letter's next item turns to the progress of the Plan. Retain mandatorily with the supplied reference.

importedAuthorityReview.authorization: Provisional translation of a paragraph whose authorized rendering is separately selected.
importedAuthorityReview.finding: The supplied text identifies itself as a provisional translation published in Bahai Ethics. BH00041 version e7bcab9b7dfeb947cdfc71a986c72bdb47aa1c4f1d2399837032db2b9a5f3a37 paragraph34, metadata Y34,36, gives the authorized wording Detachment is as the sun; in whatsoever heart it doth shine it quencheth the fire of covetousness and self, which is already selected. Omit the provisional variant.

importedAuthorityReview.authorization: Verified authorized Gleanings section CXXVIII wording.
importedAuthorityReview.finding: Read Gleanings from the Writings of Bahaullah section CXXVIII at the linked official page: Disencumber yourselves of all attachment to this world and the vanities thereof. Beware that ye approach them not, inasmuch as they prompt you to walk after your own lusts and covetous desires, and hinder you from entering the straight and glorious Path. The supplied wording agrees exactly. The catalogue candidate BH00144 paragraph17 is a different provisional rendering of the Suriy-i-Bayan without authorization and is not substituted. Retain mandatorily and preserve approximate status.

importedAuthorityReview.authorization: Authorized Ishraqat paragraph38, with one supplied word difference preserved.
importedAuthorityReview.finding: Compared BH00053 version04c46858729333014a706175200de21f90a583ae3722c7e119fc3f3146bf154c paragraph38, metadata Y, and the official Tablets of Bahaullah page. The authorized sentence, following The Tablet is ended, but the theme is unexhausted, reads Be patient, for thy Lord is patient; the supplied wording has the Lord. Include conservatively for the authorized sentence without adopting the variant word, and preserve approximate status.

importedAuthorityReview.authorization: Quran3:200 in an unidentified English rendering; Bahai translation-authorization metadata does not apply.
importedAuthorityReview.finding: The linked primary page gives Quran3:200 with a modern translation: O believers! Patiently endure, persevere, stand on guard, and be mindful of Allah, so you may be successful. The supplied be patient, vie in patience, persevere is a different rendering of the same verse; its translator is not identified. Include as an original comparative selection with the supplied wording.

importedAuthorityReview.authorization: Christian mystical text; supplied translator unidentified, no Bahai translation authority.
importedAuthorityReview.finding: The supplied reference names Ascent of Mount Carmel Book3 chapter26. The supplied wording was not compared with an identified English edition during selection review, so its translator remains unverified. Omit; the guide’s own passages on love independent of reward cover this theme.

importedAuthorityReview.authorization: Christian mystical letter; supplied translator unidentified, no Bahai translation authority.
importedAuthorityReview.finding: The Kavanaugh–Rodriguez Collected Works letter13 contains the corresponding teaching that those are foolish who think God is failing them for lack of spiritual sweetness, in wording different from the supplied Letter XI translation. The supplied translator has not been identified. Omit; the guide keeps its comparative selections to two short scriptural sayings.

integrationReview.decision: The distinction between infant incapacity and mature detachment adds a necessary qualification beyond the familiar two-wings image.
